caption: The bond was R7 900 but the house is R14 000. Did anyone warn you about the extras?

slides.title:
What my first home
really costs me
on R27 500 p/m
South Africa
Living in Brakpan
slides.body:
Female, 30
Single, bought her first home last year
Job: Dental hygienist
Net salary: R27 500 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.body: The bank said I could afford more. I'm glad I didn't test it.

slides.title: Rates, levies & water
slides.includes: Municipal rates, body corporate levy, water
slides.body: The levy goes up every year and I'm told I'll love the new paving.

slides.title: Repairs & fixing
slides.includes: Geyser element, burglar bars, a leaking tap that wasn't just a tap
slides.body: Nobody told me a house charges you a surprise every month. Renting never did.

slides.title: Electricity
slides.includes: Prepaid, plus a small inverter for the fridge and router
slides.body: Load shedding taught me that the fibre router is the first thing I protect.

slides.title: Security & home insurance
slides.body: I read the policy twice. It's still confusing.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Groceries, car instalment, petrol, medical aid, phone, funeral policy, stokvel
slides.body: The car is R3 300 of this. I'd love to say I'm paying the bond harder instead.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R27 500. The house costs R14 000 a month before I've bought a single grocery.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I put the bond, levy and repairs into Beyond Horizon as one budget so I could see what the house really costs.

The repairs line is the one that kept growing.

No bank login needed.
